pr_title: [Pod Security] Baseline + restricted policy checks for seccomp
pr_body:
#### What type of PR is this?

/kind feature

#### What this PR does / why we need it:

This PR adds a restricted policy check for seccomp profiles.

#### Which issue(s) this PR fixes:

Fixes #103205
Fixes #103388

#### Special notes for your reviewer:

This is a tentative PR, but would like some clarification. From the issue:

> - generateFail should generate test cases
>   - pod that doesn't set any seccomp profile (**default is unconfined**)

Would it make sense to create a helper similar to `ensureSELinuxOptions` to create this default seccomp profile? I attempted that, but was getting tons of errors relating to other restricted policy tests (ie not seccomp related). For the time being, I don't have a "minimal valid pod" test that would trigger this error.

#### Does this PR introduce a user-facing change?

```release-note
NONE
```

#### Additional documentation e.g., KEPs (Kubernetes Enhancement Proposals), usage docs, etc.:

```docs
- [KEP]: https://git.k8s.io/enhancements/keps/sig-auth/2579-psp-replacement
```

/sig auth security

In its current state, this PR adds a new way to register fixture generators:

```go
newFixtureRegistration("seccomp").
	baseline(api.MajorMinorVersion(1, 0), fixtureData_baseline).
	restricted(api.MajorMinorVersion(1, 0), fixtureData_restricted)
```

The underlying code is pretty much the same, except _baseline fixtures aren't copied into the restricted folder._ This addresses an issue I had when trying to test seccomp at both baseline and restricted levels. Waiting to hear if this issue occurs with the capabilities checks (and if this approach will fix that issue)

Could potentially be back-ported to other checks that rely on copying fixture generators with something like:

```go
newFixtureRegistration("my-check").
	nonprivileged(api.MajorMinorVersion(1, 0), fixtureData)
```

But I kinda prefer defining levels explicitly

Also worth noting that [pull-kubernetes-unit](https://prow.k8s.io/view/gs/kubernetes-jenkins/pr-logs/pull/103341/pull-kubernetes-unit/1412110759571230720) is failing because this PR has to update all previously-existing fixtures to include the seccomp info.

@tallclair how do we resolve this?

> The underlying code is pretty much the same, except _baseline fixtures aren't copied into the restricted folder._

We intentionally kept baseline and restricted checks for the same fields having unique IDs, to be positive that the restricted level was strictly additive over baseline.

in general, I think we still want the baseline check fixtures in the restricted testdata folders, but I would recommend inspecting the minimal restricted pod to see if it has seccomp options already in the baseline generatePass function... if it does, it can simply return the minimal valid pod (or return nil once https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/103517 merges). That will let the baseline fixtures co-exist with the restricted check on the same field

issue_context.title: [PodSecurity] baseline - seccomp: forbid explicit unconfined
issue_context.body:
Runtimes (cri-o & containerd) let you override the default seccomp profile, and there is a new proposal to change the default profile (https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/tree/master/keps/sig-node/2413-seccomp-by-default). To respect these changes to the default in the baseline profile, we should forbid _explicitly_ setting the seccomp profile to unconfined.

Note: this is different from the restricted check, which _requires_ the profile to be **set** to something other than unconfined.
comments:

it should be its own check
